authored_by: coordinator, before any clustering code existed
purpose: This fixture is the acceptance gate for the clustering engine (packet C1).
It is authored deliberately BEFORE the implementation and must not be edited
to make an implementation pass. A validator that grades its own homework is
the failure family this repository exists to catalogue.
Every member ID below was verified present in pipeline/L1/*.jsonl at authoring
time. These families were identified by independent human-directed reading of
the source corpus, NOT by any clustering algorithm -- that is what makes them

families.claim: A process, agent or tool reports that work finished; the artifact it claims to have produced does not exist, or the process is dead, zombied, or still running.
families.why_it_matters: The single most-repeated lesson in the corpus. Re-logged at least 7 times in 3 weeks under 7 different IDs, each treated as a new discovery.
families.note: fleet-OPS-11 and fleet-orch-OPS-11 are the same failure recorded in two separate files -- a cross-file duplicate that a correct clusterer must also collapse.

families.claim: Two or more concurrent agents or dispatches operate in one working tree or checkout and observe or clobber each other's uncommitted state; evidence that appears independent is not.
families.why_it_matters: Seven separate incidents spanning 2026-07-14 to 2026-07-30, each logged as a fresh discovery of the identical root cause.

families.claim: A gate collapses error and reject into one channel, so a dependency failure, a 404, or an exit-0-on-error path is read as a passing or rejecting verdict rather than as a broken check.
families.why_it_matters: Logged 4 times under different IDs before the chapters were merged under CI-1.

families.claim: A deduplication or identity key is coupled to the discoverer or to surface phrasing, so equivalent items never collapse -- or an escape hatch added to fix that then over-merges genuinely distinct items.
families.why_it_matters: Relearned three times on the same source file, chaptered a/b/c.
families.note: Self-referential: this is the failure mode the clusterer under test could itself commit.

families.claim: Multiple reviewers or lanes agree because they share one upstream source, not because they independently verified; or a claim/gap is asserted with no negative-search artifact behind it.
families.why_it_matters: ORC-9 and ORC-11 are the same failure eleven days apart; ORC-11 cites ORC-9 by name as the same root class.

recall.rule: For each family, its members must land in a single cluster.
recall.rationale: Allows one outlier per large family without permitting the family to fragment. A family whose members scatter across clusters means the engine cannot see recurrence, which is the entire deliverable.

precision.rule: No two families listed below may be merged into the same cluster.
precision.rationale: Recall alone is trivially satisfiable by putting the whole corpus in one cluster. Precision is what makes the recall assertion meaningful. Both must hold.

headline.rule: The completion-signal cluster must be reported with a recurrence count of at least 6 distinct member entries.
headline.rationale: This is the project's stated ground-truth test. If the pipeline cannot independently rediscover the most-repeated lesson in the corpus, its output must not be trusted and downstream synthesis must not proceed.

backend_agnostic.rule: These assertions must hold for whichever embedding backend is active -- the HTTP embedding service or the numpy TF-IDF fallback.
backend_agnostic.rationale: The fallback is not a lesser mode that may quietly fail the contract. If it cannot meet the bar it must fail loudly, not degrade silently.
